hypothesis: Two real cases where boundary extraction needed phasing will indicate the build-trigger; skill-use log helps measure when this fires.
summary: A planning skill for staged boundary decoupling. Consumes a staging-decision-framework ADR + an /impact-feature output + a /propose-boundary artifact, then produces a phase-graph (nodes = phases, edges = predecessors) with phase-boundary verification gates and partial-revert plans. Build only after the staging-decision-framework ADR lands AND a real boundary extraction surfaces a P0 staging fork.
title: /plan-phased-refactor skill for staged decoupling

hypothesis: Coherence drift can be measured by cross-package change-amplification + cross-package import directionality + concept fingerprint overlap. Open question whether this rolls up cleanly enough to be actionable.
summary: Higher-abstraction analog to SOLID: detects when a system as a whole drifts from internal coherence. Cousin to /find-folder-topology-drift but at the system-of-subsystems level. Candidate signals: concepts fighting across modules, subsystem boundaries dissolved by features that cross them, change-amplification that crosses package walls.
title: System-coherence drift detector

summary: Backfill skill-use logging across every existing skill rather than opt-in-as-touched. Would give immediate full coverage but requires touching every skill's terminal stage. Trade-off: speed of evidence accumulation vs upfront instrumentation cost. Engineering-skills owns this question since the shared library is where skills land first.
title: Retroactive skill-use logging across existing ecosystem

hypothesis: Grouping by job (find/propose/refactor/map/decide/track/extract/etc.) will surface seams that motivate orchestration layers and reveal which large skills are split-candidates.
summary: Apply folder-organization conventions (>=3-sibling packaging threshold; see host project decision registry) to .claude/skills/. Today's catalog is flat (~30+ skills); natural groups exist (find-* / propose-* / refactor-* / map-* / decide / track-*). The conventions codified for the codebase should apply to the skill ecosystem itself.
title: Apply folder-organization rules to .claude/skills/

summary: Hash vs verbatim target paths; retention/rotation policy beyond the basic compaction-and-archive mechanism; commit-gate criteria for the active log. Defer until log size or commit pressure makes the question concrete. The compaction mechanism handles growth but not privacy.
title: Skill-use log privacy and retention policy

hypothesis: There is a missing midpoint between '/refactor-subsystem extracts N files' and 'leave it bad': a single-file reorganizer that clusters symbols by domain, adds banner comments + a top-of-file index, declares __all__, and emits no semantic changes. Many 1K-LOC omnibuses are tolerable when sensibly organized; not all need extraction.
origin: Conversation in host project 2026-05-14 on omnibus follow-up options
summary: Skill that takes an omnibus file as input and produces a structurally-reorganized version with: (1) symbol clustering by domain (reuse the same head-noun clustering /find-omnibus uses), (2) section banner comments grouping each cluster, (3) a top-of-file index/TOC docstring, (4) an explicit __all__ declaration listing the public API in order, (5) zero semantic changes. Default --require-recent-edits gate skips files with no edits in 90+ days unless --force ('leave stable files alone'). Outputs a --dry-run move plan first. Tooling caveat: a whole-file reorder buries git-blame trails — mitigated by 'git log --follow' / 'git blame -w -CC' which preserve authorship across moves; report should hint at these flags. Slots into the maintenance loop as a sibling to /refactor-subsystem: /find-omnibus → DECISION (decompose | reorganize | leave) → /refactor-subsystem OR /organize-file OR skip. Composes with: /propose-boundary (when reorg surfaces a clean seam, re-evaluate as a refactor candidate); the staged-boundary ADR (refuse-phasing rules apply if a reorg unexpectedly grows into a refactor).
title: /organize-file — reorganize an omnibus without restructuring

hypothesis: Two-token prefix or verb-stripping logic would surface the obviously-correct seams that humans see immediately. The current single-token approach is too eager to collapse.
summary: Naming clusters use first-token-after-generic-verb-strip as cluster key. e.g. 'save_html_to_file' and 'save_screenshot_to_file' both land in the 'save_*' cluster, but the real semantic cluster is 'file I/O' (which also wants 'url_to_filename'). The skill misses obvious file-I/O / crawl / discovery clusters when the head-noun is generic. Candidate fix: two-token prefix OR head-noun-after-verb extraction. Evidence: a real shared-helper file showed 3 weak prefix seams while manual reading shows >=3 strong semantic clusters.
title: /propose-boundary naming clusters are single-token-prefix only

hypothesis: Most real targets have lifetime > 90 days; the default should reflect that. A loud empty-signal warning + auto-widening would prevent silent quality degradation.
summary: Default --co-edit-days=90 returns 0 co-edit pairs for active code if all activity is older than the window (or the file was renamed and git log doesn't follow rename). Candidate seams then score co_edit_intensity=0.00; only naming signal carries. Candidate fixes: (a) default to 180+ days, (b) make window relative to file mtime, (c) warn loudly when co-edit signal is empty so the human knows naming-only scores are weaker evidence.
title: /propose-boundary co-edit signal empty when target has no recent git history

hypothesis: Every project with the Claude harness will have .claude/worktrees/ pollution. A default skip-glob is high-value, near-zero risk.
summary: Proposal for a shared helper listed ~150 importers; ~80% were duplicates from stale agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-*. These worktrees contain old copies of the codebase. Inflates importer counts, dilutes 'callers_into_private_helpers', and makes the report harder to scan. Candidate fix: ship with default --skip-path-glob '.claude/worktrees/**' (and maybe also '**/.venv/**' though Python AST should not import .venv anyway). Trivial change; broad impact.
title: /propose-boundary should default-skip .claude/worktrees/

hypothesis: find-omnibus already solved this with a JSON+md split; mirroring that pattern is the right move.
summary: --output accepts any path including X.md but writes a JSON data dump (multi-MB for nontrivial targets). Misleading filename suggests human-readable markdown. Candidate fixes: (a) rename flag to --output-json (consistent with find-omnibus's --output-md / --output-json split), (b) add a markdown renderer that consumes the JSON and produces a scannable report — same pattern as find-omnibus's report.py. (b) is the better fix because it preserves machine-readable data for downstream skills while also giving humans a readable surface.
title: /propose-boundary --output X.md writes JSON, not markdown

hypothesis: Augment the report with either (a) a verb-phrase summary per cluster ('formats *', 'sanitizes *') instead of bare nouns, or (b) a 5-line head-of-file summary the skill prompts the user to write before deciding. Either way, the cluster-name column should not be the primary disambiguator — risk score plus a one-line semantic hint should be.
summary: Top-N omnibus shortlist showed cluster names that didn't match the real concerns of the file. A high-LOC export file reported clusters as 'iter, export, notes, flatteneddata' — but the architect-skim concerns were dimension-formatting, image-sanitization, cross-DB JOIN, and downstream wiring. The detector picks the most frequent head-nouns, not the semantically distinct concerns. Result: humans have to open the file to know whether decompose vs reorganize is the right call.
title: /propose-boundary cluster names hide intent on dense files

hypothesis: Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' is a Python idiom; every Python project with refactors will eventually hit this bit-rot. The skill is one of the cheapest guardrails available.
summary: Host project shipped a /find-broken-file-refs skill (advisory SUSPECT scan for Python Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' expressions whose target doesn't exist on disk). Catches refactor-induced bit-rot in self-anchored asset paths. SKILL.md currently references Django render() in not_for; needs scrubbing for the engineering-skills mirror (Python-general, framework-agnostic). Pairs with ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification). Skill scope is universally applicable to any Python codebase with relocatable modules + literal-asset paths.
title: Mirror /find-broken-file-refs skill (host: pnci-pricing → engineering-skills)

hypothesis: Asset-path bit-rot is a universal Python refactor failure mode. A template ADR + the suspect skill together close it cheaply.
summary: Host project shipped ADR 0015: every Python file move must prove Path(__file__) constants still resolve. Decision is anchored by two real production incidents where modules moved a directory deeper and their .parent chain silently resolved to the wrong location, with the failure surfacing only at runtime. Engineering-skills mirror should be the template form (decision sections present, concrete N thresholds/incident IDs replaced with placeholders for adopters to fill in). Pairs with /find-broken-file-refs intake and /refactor-subsystem Phase 6.0.5 gate.
title: Mirror ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification) as a template

hypothesis: The 5th-tier migration was per-skill (not bulk). propose-boundary was probably migrated in engineering-skills first; the host fork needs a one-line catchup.
summary: Cross-direction sync finding: engineering-skills propose-boundary/scripts/propose.py uses the centralized _common/skill_use.py log_event helper, but host project pnci-pricing's version still has the older local _log_skill_use function. This means at least one host hasn't yet completed the skill-use 5th-tier migration. Either (a) host pnci-pricing should update propose-boundary's script to use _common/skill_use.py, or (b) engineering-skills should retain compatibility for hosts still on the pre-centralization helper. Captured here for visibility; the actual sync may be a one-line edit in the host's script.
title: Host propose-boundary script still has local skill-use logger (pre-_common migration)

hypothesis: An atlas authored once saves the manual Explore-agent passes that real-project observational synthesis tends to require. Provides L3 input surface that /propose-boundary lacks.
summary: Produces a one-page project atlas: one line per top-level subsystem with shape, dependents, dependencies, co-edit neighbors, importance-map tier. Sibling to /map-subsystem at one abstraction higher (L3 instead of L2). Output feeds /propose-boundary (with --scope=project, if added) and /propose-architecture (when that lands). Possible overlap with /propose-folder-reorganization — needs scoping pass first to clarify whether to extend that skill or build separately. Natural output home: a .claude/docs/atlas.md surface authored once + refreshed periodically.
title: /map-project skill — project-level atlas (L3 abstraction)

hypothesis: Without an authored constraints surface, any architecture-level proposal skill will hallucinate vendor-coupling, hot-path assertions, or team-ownership facts. With the surface, a small skill can produce highly contextual recommendations. Pilot: declare one entry, then validate downstream skill output reflects it.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Authored surface declaring architectural constraints the code alone can't reveal: (1) tight-integration zones (vendor-coupled code that shouldn't be abstracted — the file's value is co-location of vendor quirks); (2) hot paths (where network hops between modules are unacceptable); (3) failure domains (independent-failure modules, circuit-breakable); (4) team ownership (multi-team adopters). Possibly extends importance-map.md (ADR 0016) as new locator kinds, or a sibling constraints-map.md. Prerequisite for /propose-architecture — completion-trained models will fabricate these signals if not given them.
title: constraints-declaration-surface — authored inputs for constraint-aware architecture

hypothesis: The most valuable architecture insights come from the disagreement between lenses, not from either alone. A skill that surfaces disagreement is much higher-leverage than either lens alone.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Higher-abstraction sibling to /propose-boundary. Consumes project atlas (from /map-project) + constraints-declaration-surface, produces three-bucket output: (1) structural-clean seams to act on; (2) structural seams to leave coupled with constraint rationale (vendor-coupling, hot-path proximity, failure-domain co-location); (3) deployment-seam candidates (microservice / library / separate-repo) with constraint evidence (distinct scaling profile, independent failure domain, stable narrow contract, team alignment). Headline value: surfacing DISAGREEMENT between structural and constraint lenses (e.g. 'structural says split, constraint says encapsulate'). Output framed as evidence for a System-tier deliberation chain, not a verdict.
title: /propose-architecture skill — constraint-aware optimal-shape proposal

hypothesis: Multi-team adopters will hit Conway's-Law boundary questions immediately on adoption. An /propose-architecture run with a team-ownership map should produce visibly different recommendations than the same run without one.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on team-organization in boundary design
summary: Explicit orthogonal-concern intake for team-ownership boundaries. Conway's Law: organizations design systems mirroring their communication structures. When multiple teams own slices of a codebase, optimal boundaries follow team lines to minimize coordination tax — sometimes overriding structural cleanliness. Inverse case (two teams stepping on one file) is a coordination-tax signal that argues for splitting even when the structural seam is messier. Critical for multi-team adopters; degenerate for single-team projects. Likely shape: a field within constraints-declaration-surface (kind=team-ownership locator + team name), not a separate file.
title: Conway's Law overlay — team-ownership boundaries as architecture force
